llama.raw_text: Soft tissue necrosis of the stem bark near the soil line is the first sign of the disease. A white, cottony, and silvery mycelial growth is visible on the affected area. Later, a white to light brown mustard-like sclerotium appears on the same area. The disease is soil-borne and the pathogen survives in the form of sclerotia.

Brown spots with concentric rings in a bull's eye pattern with a yellow margin. Fruit gets infected through the calyx or stem attachment. Lesions are V-shaped and progress towards the midrib. These lesions have prominent yellowing on their outer margin due to a host-specific toxin produced by the pathogen. Disease appears in the vegetative phase of the plant before flowering.

llama.raw_text: Rhizoctonia fruit rot is the most serious disease of kharif tomatoes. Symptoms appear as rhythmic rotting of fruits coming with the soil contact. Rotting is followed by cracking and fungal growth over it. Lower portion of fruits are usually infected which come into contact with the soil. To prevent the disease, keep the fruits off the soil by staking the plants. Ensure proper drainage in the field.

Sometimes clear narrow yellow halo is visible around the spots. Usually these spots are isolated but in later stage they coalesce to each other. Severely infected older leaves blight and fall down.

llama.raw_text: Young larvae feed on tender foliage. Mature larvae bore circular holes. Thrust only a part of its body into fruit and eat the inner content. Eggs hatch in about 3-4 days and the first instars larvae initially feed on the leaves and migrate to the developing green fruit later. The larvae bore into the fruits with the posterior end outside the hole.

llama.raw_text: Root-knot nematodes cause root galls on the feeder roots and sometimes affect the entire root system showing heavy galling. This affects the uptake of nutrition and water and the plants show wilting during the warmer part of the day. This causes stunted plants with yellow foliage resulting in yield reduction. Infected plants in patches in the field. Formation of galls on the host root system is the primary symptom. Roots branch profusely starting from the gall tissue causing a 'beard root' symptom. Infected roots become knobby and knotty. In severely infected plants the root system is reduced and the rootlets are almost completely absent. The roots are seriously hampered in their function of uptake and transport of water and nutrients.

llama.raw_text: Chlorotic spots appear on tomato leaves. Yellowing occurs on tomato leaves. Downward curling and drying of leaves happen on tomato leaves. Whitefly is a well-known vector that transmits tomato leaf curl virus. Whiteflies have piercing and sucking mouthparts and both nymphs and adults feed on the lower surface of the leaves, causing deformation of young leaves. Whiteflies also excrete honeydew, which causes sooty mold. Remove Abutilon indicum from the area. Uproot and destroy the diseased leaf curl plants. Use nitrogen and irrigation judiciously. Raise nurseries in seedling trays under nylon nets or polyhouses.
